name: Contradiction Resolution
description: Belief revision under contradiction. Inspired by BeliefShift (arXiv 2603.23848). Adapters must converge on the corrected belief once a contradicting observation arrives, even after the prior belief was reinforced multiple times.

scenarios.title: A reinforced vendor selection is overturned by a board decision

events.content: The DataPipeline team initially selected Northwind as the analytics vendor based on the original RFP scoring.
Architecture review confirmed Northwind for the DataPipeline analytics layer because of its existing connector for the staging warehouse.
Procurement attached Northwind's preferred-vendor agreement to the DataPipeline analytics scope of work.
The board overturned the analytics vendor decision and switched the DataPipeline vendor to Southspar, citing data residency and the new compliance program.
Engineering published a Southspar onboarding runbook for the DataPipeline analytics migration after the board's vendor switch.

probes.query: Which analytics vendor should the DataPipeline team be onboarding now?
What runbook should new engineers follow for the DataPipeline analytics integration this month?

scenarios.title: A reinforced security policy is reverted by an incident review

events.content: AdminAuth keys were originally rotated every 30 days under the launch hardening policy.
The internal security wiki cited the 30-day AdminAuth rotation cadence as the canonical setting.
The on-call runbook listed 30-day AdminAuth key rotation as a routine operation step.
After the AdminAuth credential leak post-mortem, the security incident review tightened AdminAuth key rotation to every 7 days and made the prior 30-day cadence non-compliant.

probes.query: How often should AdminAuth keys be rotated under the current security policy?
